whyUs.title: Autonomous Innovation
whyUs.desc: The fastest growing and most innovative engineering design team at UBC Okanagan; the only team working on autonomous subsea robotics technology.

whyUs.title: Full-Stack Engineering
whyUs.desc: From custom multi-layer PCB design and deep learning computer vision to hydrodynamic hull simulation, our members build industry-grade subsea systems.

whyUs.title: Collaborative Culture
whyUs.desc: Fueled by deep curiosity and rigorous collaboration. Every member contributes directly to competition vehicles and mission-critical hardware.

whyUs.title: World-Class Mentorship
whyUs.desc: Partnered with premier marine defense and subsea technology leaders like Cellula Robotics and Blue Trail Engineering for hands-on mentorship.

faqs.a: The Marine Robotics Team provides the unique opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology and a passionate multidisciplinary team. It allows you to gain real-world design, fabrication, and testing experience while building connections with leading subsea industry professionals.

faqs.q: Do I need to have experience to join?
faqs.a: No prior robotics experience is required! We welcome eager learners. We provide mentorship, workshops, and hands-on projects so anyone with enthusiasm can develop their technical skills.

faqs.q: What if I'm not an Engineering student?
faqs.a: We welcome students from all faculties! In addition to electrical, mechanical, and computer engineering, our team relies on computer science, management, finance, physics, psychology, and media students.
Typical commitment ranges from 3 to 10 hours per week depending on your role, subteam, and competition deadlines. We are flexible, so you can commit as many or as few hours as you want.

faqs.q: What is the most important thing I should know before joining?
faqs.a: Curiosity, consistency, and a desire to collaborate are the keys to success on our team. We love initiative and proactive problem solvers!
You can apply during our fall and winter recruitment cycles through our linktree or send an email directly to okmarinerobotics@gmail.com with your interests!
